title: Getting along with the white community in Natchez
summary: McAllister describes himself as quiet and well liked by white people who helped him get work.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: What, uh, when do you think you heard what seemed to you to be jazz? Do you have any idea? The earliest time?

Well, no sir, I don't. After I let the music along, I got the, you know, young fella getting wild and I, uh, sit up by being a, I guess, pretty quiet fella here in my hometown. I don't know, it seems like that, uh, if I have to say it with you gentlemen, sure, that, uh, I was a pretty quiet fella and I was pretty well liked by all of the white people. I never had anything very much, but they always made things convenient for me. But I was just a straightforward colored fella and up until this present moment now. I never had no big jobs to pay very much, but I made quite a bit of money. And all that was gave to me. It was gave to me by your people, so it's no use in me saying anything against that. They would gave me, get out of anything. Mitch, what do you think you can do? Well, what do you want? We'll open up your place. But I was a straightforward fella with it. I done right. They gave me everything.
